title: Enterprise Onboarding: Support, Integration, Known Issues & QBR Playbook
author: Marina Gonzalez
body:
Overview
========
This playbook consolidates enterprise onboarding steps, the escalation path, integration checklist, known issues & workarounds, and health-check / QBR materials used by Customer Success (CS) and Support teams. It is intended for CS, Solutions Engineering, Support L2/L3, and SRE owners.

Scope
-----
- New enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private deployments)
- Migration customers moving from hosted to Dedicated/Private
- Existing customers onboarding significant new workloads or integrations

Key outcomes
------------
- Customer is production-ready with validated connectivity, monitoring, and rollout plan
- Clear ownerable escalation path with SLOs and SLAs for response and resolution
- Documented integration checklist and known issues to expedite resolution
- Standardized QBR agenda and health-check metrics for recurring business reviews

1) Roles and ownership
----------------------
- Customer Success (CS): Primary onboarding owner, weekly check-ins, QBR facilitation
- Solutions Engineering (SE): Integration design, API verification, test prompts
- Support L2: Triage, logs, initial remediation, runbook execution
- Support L3 / Eng: Code/runtime fixes, model-serving investigations, kernel/quantization issues
- SRE / Infra: Capacity, networking, and incident response for platform faults

Contact matrix (example)
----------------------
1. CS Owner: cs-owner@redwood.ai (primary)
2. SE Lead: se-lead@redwood.ai (integration issues)
3. Support Oncall: support-oncall@redwood.ai (24/7)
4. SRE Pager: pagerduty (severity >= P1)

2) Enterprise onboarding checklist (high level)
------------------------------------------------
- Pre-engagement
  1. NDA & contract signed; confirm deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
  2. Kickoff meeting: objectives, success criteria, timeline, stakeholders
- Technical prep (SE + SRE)
  1. Network & firewall requirements validated (see table below)
  2. Capacity sizing & reserved instance plan agreed
  3. API keys & RBAC roles provisioned
  4. Data residency & retention policy confirmed
- Integration & validation
  1. Test prompts and evaluation harness run (sanity, latency, cost)
  2. End-to-end telemetry enabled (traces, token-level cost)
  3. Failure modes validated (timeouts, fallbacks, model variant routing)
- Cutover & handoff
  1. Canary rollout plan with rollback criteria
  2. Support runbook shared; escalation contacts verified
  3. Post-cutover 72-hour monitoring window and daily check-ins

Networking & minimum port requirements (table)
------------------------------------------------
- Allowed outbound: TCP 443 to *.redwood-inference.com (API endpoints)
- VPC peering / private links: CIDR ranges, BGP sessions as required
- MTU: 1500 (recommend)
- Minimum bandwidth: 100 Mbps per 8 concurrent model instances (adjust per workload)

3) Integration guide (SE checklist)
----------------------------------
- Pre-reqs: API key, assigned role, telemetry endpoint, sample dataset (1000 prompts)
- Steps:
  1. Validate API connectivity: curl https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
  2. Run sample generation against chosen model(s) and measure baseline latency and tokens per second (TPS)
  3. Configure streaming vs non-streaming based on application UX
  4. Enable prefix caching for high-reuse workloads (CS/SE to advise cache keys)
  5. Confirm model pinning & fallback policy in deployment config
- Deliverables:
  - Integration test report (latency, p50/p95, token cost)
  - Security checklist signed by customer security contact

4) Escalation playbook (triage & escalation matrix)
--------------------------------------------------
- Severity definitions:
  - P1 (Sev 1): Complete service outage or customer-critical path failure impacting production revenue; 15 min response, 2 hour workaround or mitigation plan
  - P2: Significant degradation (latency > 5x SLO, widespread errors); 30 min response, 8 hour mitigation plan
  - P3: Functional bug with workaround; 4 hour response, SLA-aligned fix window
- Escalation matrix:
  1. Customer reports to Support (support@redwood.ai) or via portal -> Support L2 triage
  2. L2 gathers logs, request/response samples, job IDs, and reproducer; attempt standard runbooks
  3. If unresolved within severity-specific timeframe, L2 escalates to Support L3 and notifies SE and CS owner
  4. For infra/resource-related issues, escalate to SRE and activate on-call rotation
  5. For contractual/BI/entitlement issues, involve Customer Success Manager and Legal/Finance as needed
- Required artifacts on escalation:
  - Request/response samples (redact PII)
  - Trace IDs, token/latency graphs, model version and quantization profile
  - Reproduction steps or synthetic test case

5) Known issues & workarounds (selection)
------------------------------------------
- Symptom: High p95 latency on long-context chat with quantized 4-bit model
  - Workaround: Temporarily switch to FP16 or lower-context quantized profile; enable KV cache warmup; increase batch size for throughput-focused endpoints
- Symptom: Occasional OOM in Dedicated pool during burst load
  - Workaround: Enable per-instance memory throttling and route bursts to lower-cost regional pool; schedule workload smoothing via rate limits
- Symptom: API returns 401 intermittently after key rotation
  - Workaround: Confirm client key caching TTL < key rotation window; recommend exponential backoff and key refresh before expiry
- Symptom: Embeddings mismatch between model variants
  - Workaround: Standardize on a single embeddings model per index rebuild and use deterministic seeding for tokenizer preprocessing

6) Support process & SLAs
-------------------------
- Standard SLA targets for enterprise customers (subject to contract):
  - Response times: P1 15m, P2 30m, P3 4h
  - Target resolution times: P1 4h, P2 24h, P3 7d (depending on root cause)
- Support workflow:
  1. Customer opens ticket via portal or email -> auto-acknowledge
  2. L1 triage (automated scripts): Check API keys, identity, and quota
  3. Assign to L2 for deeper triage; attach diagnostics checklist
  4. Escalate to L3 or Eng if required; update customer every SLA window

7) Health checks & QBR materials
--------------------------------
- Weekly health check (CS-led)
  - Dashboard: per-route latency (p50/p95), token consumption, error rate, cache hit rate, billing delta vs forecast
  - Action items: throttling adjustments, model recommendation changes, cost optimization suggestions
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template
  - Agenda:
    1. Executive summary (uptime, major incidents, ROI summary)
    2. Usage trends and cost analysis (tokens by route, unit cost)
    3. Model quality & regression summary (evals run, notable changes)
    4. Roadmap & product updates relevant to customer
    5. Open action items and next steps
  - Required slides / artifacts:
    - Incident review summaries (since last QBR)
    - Performance & cost trend charts (90d)
    - Proposed optimizations with estimated savings

8) Post-onboarding 90-day cadence
----------------------------------
- 0–30 days: Daily standups with SE and CS; incident watch; complete integration test suite
- 30–60 days: Weekly check-ins; cost optimizations implemented; first health-check report
- 60–90 days: Bi-weekly check-ins; QBR prep; finalize long-term runbooks and SLOs

Appendix: Runbook snippets
-------------------------
- L2 quick triage checklist:
  1. Confirm customer account & model version
  2. Pull traces for request IDs from the last 60 minutes
  3. Check per-route token billing and spikes
  4. Reproduce in staging with identical prompt & model config
  5. If reproduction succeeds, collect heap/metrics and escalate to L3
